Subject: Admin activity logs — raw export & legal hold questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're working through the SIG and SOC 2 evidence requests and have a couple of specific asks around admin activity / operator logs:

1) What exactly is captured in the admin activity stream (events, metadata, user_id vs email, API keys, IPs, resource identifiers)?
2) What's the canonical export format you can provide for a full raw export (ndjson, Parquet, CSV)?
3) Do you apply sampling or aggregation to admin/operator events by default? If so, how can we get an unsampled snapshot for audit purposes?
4) We need to place a legal hold on the account for a subset of logs (date range + user IDs). Can you confirm enforcement and retention extension options and any chain-of-custody artifacts you provide?

I've attached the SIG questionnaire excerpt that flags these items (SIG_questionnaire_v2.pdf). Our auditor also wants an estimate for turnaround time and estimated size for a 90-day raw export for a medium-sized tenant (approx. 5k reqs/day).

Appreciate any detail you can share — Emily

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Admin activity logs — raw export & legal hold questions

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed path forward and attachments.

What we log (high level):
- Actor identity: when available we record user email, internal operator id, or service principal id.
- Action verb and resource: create/update/delete, model id, route, deployment id.
- API context: request id, client IP (first 3 octets masked by default), user agent string, token scope.
- Timeline & outcome: timestamp (UTC), duration, response status, error stack summary.
- Config snapshot: when admin actions modify config (rollouts, routing), we capture the config diff and version id.

Export formats and delivery:
- Full raw export: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) or Parquet. Parquet is recommended for large volumes (columnar).
- Delivery: AWS S3 presigned multipart upload or cross-account role + bucket; GCS available by request; we also support pushing to your Kafka (secure connector).
- Metadata: each event includes a sequence id and monotonic offset to allow replay/ordering.

Sampling & aggregation: admin/operator events are treated as "high-fidelity" signals and are not sampled by default. We do apply lightweight retention tiering for high-volume telemetry (non-admin) but admin events are kept intact for the retention window.

Legal hold and retention extension:
- We can apply a legal hold targeted by date range + operator IDs or resource selectors. That moves matching events into a protected tier and prevents automatic deletion.
- Standard retention for admin activity (hosted tenants) is 90 days by default; legal hold can extend retention up to 7 years with appropriate contract addendum.
- Chain-of-custody: exports include a manifest with MD5 and SHA256 checksums, signed export metadata (timestamped and signed by our export service), and an audit trail showing who requested each export.

Redaction & PII:
- We support configurable redaction at export time: deterministic pseudonymization for email/username fields (HMAC with customer-specific salt), or full redaction.
- Raw exports for audits can be produced either with redactions applied or with a privacy-preserving hash mapping file provided under an additional NDA.

Turnaround & sizing:
- For a 90-day export at ~5k admin events/day (small-medium), expect ~500MB-2GB ndjson depending on payloads. Typical delivery SLAs: 3 business days to prepare and deliver a snapshot; expedited 24-48h possible with approval.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm exact selectors (date range, user ids, resource filters).
2) Decide on export format and redaction policy.
3) We'll create a scoped export request (internal ticket) and provide a delivery plan + S3 bucket details.

I've attached a short export options playbook (admin_export_playbook.pdf) with the steps and sample manifests. Looping in Monica to own the export coordination and Rishi for security specifics.

— Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — that's very helpful. A couple of follow-ups:

- For chain-of-custody we need signed attestations showing the export was produced by Redwood and an unmodified copy delivered to our bucket. The auditor prefers SHA256 manifests and a signed export metadata file. Looks like you already provide those — can you add an example manifest to the playbook?
- For legal hold enforcement, does Redwood notify us prior to any retention policy changes? We want to ensure holds are visible in an admin UI and auditable.
- On redaction: we need a deterministic approach since the auditor will want to link operator IDs across systems. HMAC with a salt under our control would work. Can your export pipeline accept a customer-provided salt?

I'll confirm the selectors (date range + three internal operator IDs) once we align on process.

-Appreciate it, Emily

Subject: Re: Admin activity logs — raw export & legal hold questions

Emily — happy to jump in with the security specifics. A few technical notes that might help your auditor and implementation team: 

1) Manifest and signing: our export service produces a manifest.jsonl with per-file SHA256 and size, plus a top-level export_metadata.json which contains the export id, requester, selectors, and a service-generated signature (RSA-2048) timestamped by our HSM-backed signing service. We'll include a sample manifest in admin_export_playbook.pdf (attached).

2) Deterministic pseudonymization: we support HMAC-SHA256 using a customer-supplied salt (recommended) or a Redwood-managed salt. If you supply the salt, we perform HMAC at export time and do not retain the raw reversible mapping in our systems. You must provide the salt via secure upload (KMS envelope or a short-lived secret).

3) Chain-of-custody & auditability: every export action is logged as an immutable event with sequence id and requester identity. We store an export audit record (who requested, when, job status) for the legal hold period. For additional assurance we can run a signed hash stream that you can validate on receipt.

4) Retention enforcement & UI: holds are visible under the "Compliance -> Legal Holds" section in the Console; they include selectors, owner, creation timestamp, and TTL override. Holds must be created by a user with Compliance or Admin role; we can create a scoped API endpoint for your automation if needed.

5) Data transfer security: exports use server-side encryption with customer KMS (optional). Transfer uses HTTPS with mutual TLS or an S3 cross-account role; logs are preserved until the hold is released.

I'll attach the export_playbook.pdf with examples and the manifest template. If you want, we can sign a short attestation for the first export and include it in the DocuSign packet.

—Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
